newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday April 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday April 16.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Heavily armed soldiers from Italy, France and Spain secured two bridgeheads in Albania to begin protecting aid deliveries in the chaotic Balkan nation. The Albanian government warmly welcomed the arrival of the Italian-led multinational force (all).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said there were doubts on the sustainability of Italy's pensions system in the medium term and for this reason it was in need of reforms. The minister told parliament's lower house budget committee that pensions reforms worked out in 1995 would probably have to be corrected. Ciampi added the government's three-year economic target document (DPEF) will contain details relating to the planned reform of the country's social welfare system (all).
* Hard left Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said the Treasury Minister's stand left no room for talks with the coalition government over pensions reform (all).
* A report by national statistics institute ISTAT showed Italian industrial production fell 3.8 percent year-on-year in February 1997 against a rise of 3.4 percent in February 1996 (all).

* State-controlled energy group ENI said it intended to absorb its oil exploration and production unit Agip. The merger, to be approved by a shareholders meeting planned for the end of June, was aimed at increasing efficiency in the group's operation. The group also announced it would pay a 1996 dividend of 240 lire per share, compared with 215 lire in 1995 (all).

* Information technology group Olivetti reported a net loss for 1996 of 915 billion lire as annual sales fell 14.6 percent to 8.304 trillion lire. Olivetti also said it estimated its group loss before tax and before Omnitel in the first quarter of 1997 at 180 billion lire, in line with the group's budget (all).

* Davide Croff, managing director of banking group BNL, a partner in the telecoms venture Albacom, said energy giant ENI was not about to pull out of talks on an agreement with Albacom, and in fact an accord was very close (Il Sole 24 Ore).

* A survey by the OECD, the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development, showed Italy was within reach of meeting key goals laid down in the Maastricht Treaty for EMU, yet added that "substantial uncertainty" remained. OECD also said it expected a growth of Italian Gross Domestic Product of 1.3 percent in 1997, above government forecasts, with a further increase of around 2.25 percent in 1998 (Il Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
